Aerial Wildlife Survey Report 
Wildlife Management Unit 242 Aerial Ungulate Survey (2020) 
 
Background 
Wildlife Management Unit (WMU) 242 is located in east-central Alberta within the Red Deer-North Saskatchewan 
Region. The unit is adjacent to the eastern border of Elk Island National Park, Cooking Lake -Blackfoot Grazing 
Reserve and incorporates Ministik Lake Game Bird Sanctuary. The unit is approximately 1867km 2. The habitat is 
dominated by aspen parkland interspersed with native grassland and agricultural land and includes Beaverhill Lake. 
The most recent previous aerial ungulate survey conducted in this unit used the strip transect survey method and 
was conducted in 2013. Results of previous surveys are summarized in Tables 1-3. 
 
The objective of the survey conducted in January 2020 was to assess the status of the ungulate population in this 
WMU by determining estimates of population size, density and age-sex composition. We also recorded 
observations of additional species of interest, including carnivores, game birds, and sensitive or species at risk.  
 
Survey Method 
 
From January 8-10, 2020, a strip transect survey was conducted flying north-south lines at 1.6 km (1 mile) intervals 
resulting in 25% coverage (with 400 m wide survey strip) for a total linear survey effort of 1165 km (466 km2). Snow 
conditions were good and uniformly consistent throughout the unit. At each observation point, ungulates were 
counted by species, and, when possible, classified by sex and age. 
 
Sex and age classification was determined for moose by identification of vulva patch and size differential of 
cow/calves. Sex and age classification was determined for deer using antlers and size differential between adults and 
fawns. 
 
Density was calculated for white-tailed deer, mule deer and moose following Jolly 1969 (as described in Krebs 
2014) for surveys conducted with unequal sized units without replacement because the  transect lengths varied. 
Density was multiplied by the WMU area to determine population estimates. 90% confidence intervals were also 
calculated. A correction factor of 83% for deer detectability was applied to population and density estimates (Habib 
et al. 2012), with a factor of 95% applied to moose density and population estimates. 
 
Elk observations were recorded during the survey, but population estimates were not calculated because the 
design of this survey is not appropriate for elk population calculation. 
 
Results 
There were 881 white-tailed deer observed in 409 groups. Of the 881 white-tailed deer observed, 128 (15%) were 
bucks, 429 (49%) were does, 260 (30%) were fawns and 64 (7%) were not classified. The buck: doe ratio was 0.30 
and the fawn: doe ratio was 0.61 (Table 1). The average white-tailed deer density was estimated at 
2.21 individuals/km2. Population was estimated at 4129 (Table 1); 647 bucks, 2168 does and 1314 fawns. There 
were 242 mule deer observed within 83 groups. Of the 242 mule deer identified 45 (19%) were bucks , 121 (50%) 
were does, 76 (31%) were fawns and 0 (0%) were not classified. The buck: doe ratio was 0.37 and the fawn: doe 
ratio was 0.63 (Table 2). The average mule deer density was estimated at 0.61 individuals/km 2. Population was 
estimated at 1134 (Table 2); 211 bucks, 567 does and 356 fawns. 
 
There were 248 moose observed within 222 groups. Of the 248 moose identified, 61 (25%) were bulls, 112 (45%) 
were cows, 68 (27%) were calves and 7 (3%) were not classified. The bull:cow ratio was 0.54 and the calf:cow 
ratio was 0.61 (Table 3). The average moose density was estimated at 0.56 individuals/km 2. Population was 
estimated at 1043 (Table 3); 264 bulls, 485 cows and 294 calves.

Lastly, there were 21 elk (both on and off transect) observed within 7 gro ups. Of the 21 elk identified, 10 (48%) 
were bulls, 8 (38%) were cows, 3 (14%) were calves and 0 (0%) were not classified.  
 
We also observed 51 coyotes, 1 Great horned owl, 1 Sharp-tailed grouse and 9 Grey partridge.These are 
incidental observations only and should not be considered minimum total counts.
